dedupe_keys.name: the ray row solar mapping tool esri for highway right of way solar suitability

description: The ROW Solar mapping tool is an Esri ArcGIS Pro based tool that Esri gifted to The Ray in 2021 for assessing solar energy on highway rights-of-way owned by state departments of transportation. Coverage: advanced 3D modelling, solar radiation from digital elevation and surface models, digital twins and viewshed analysis; it ranks right-of-way areas by slope, elevation, vegetative cover and solar radiation, filters state DOT right-of-way data with exclusion and inclusion layers such as wetlands, areas near existing infrastructure and endangered species habitat, uses local or seasonal radiation data, and values the energy with local utility data and CO2 equivalents. Agencies can reshape arrays to avoid effects such as interrupted scenic views and compare scenarios. The page also links a 2020 assessment by the Webber Energy Group at UT Austin with The Ray, and notes a one-megawatt array opened in 2020 at Exit 14 of The Ray Highway in Georgia. Format and access: demonstrations for transportation agencies by email request. Licence and cost: proprietary, on request. Caveats: not a public download. The tool can size roadside generation and test siting scenarios in road corridor digital twin and capacity planning studies. It relates to the Italian highway PV study and the Global Solar Atlas in the catalogue.
